graph.summary: Methotrexate → bifunctional purine biosynthesis protein ATIC → Adenosine → inflammatory response → Rheumatoid Arthritis

evidence.snippet: intracellular MTX polyglutamates inhibit AICAR transformylase (ATIC) activity and thereby promote adenosine release
evidence.explanation: Methotrexate polyglutamates (the active intracellular form of MTX) directly inhibit ATIC activity, the enzyme encoded by the ATIC gene (UniProt:P31939), thereby decreasing its catalytic function.

paper.title: Fibroblasts from methotrexate-sensitive mice accumulate methotrexate polyglutamates but those from methotrexate-resistant mice do not.

evidence.snippet: intracellular MTX polyglutamates inhibit AICAR transformylase (ATIC) activity and thereby promote adenosine release
evidence.explanation: This snippet establishes by contrapositive that ATIC activity limits adenosine release; when ATIC is inhibited, AICAR accumulates and promotes adenosine release, confirming that active ATIC decreases adenosine abundance.

paper.title: Fibroblasts from methotrexate-sensitive mice accumulate methotrexate polyglutamates but those from methotrexate-resistant mice do not.

evidence.snippet: the pathway generating extracellular adenosine and its effects on promoting the immune regulation for the mechanism of MTX therapy of RA
evidence.explanation: Confirms that extracellular adenosine generation is the key downstream effector in MTX-treated RA patients; ATIC inhibition is the upstream step that releases this brake on adenosine abundance.

paper.title: Genetic Variants of the ATIC Gene and Therapeutic Response to Methotrexate in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis.

evidence.snippet: many of the anti-inflammatory effects of methotrexate are mediated by adenosine. This nucleoside, acting at one or more of its receptors, is a potent endogenous anti-inflammatory mediator.
evidence.explanation: Adenosine, acting via its cell-surface receptors, is a potent endogenous anti-inflammatory mediator that negatively regulates the inflammatory response; this review cites both animal and clinical studies confirming this.

paper.title: Molecular action of methotrexate in inflammatory diseases.

evidence.snippet: methotrexate increases adenosine levels and on engagement of adenosine with its extracellular receptors an intracellular cascade is activated promoting an overall anti-inflammatory state
evidence.explanation: Adenosine engagement with extracellular receptors activates an intracellular cascade that promotes an overall anti-inflammatory state, directly supporting negatively regulates inflammatory response.

paper.title: Methotrexate mechanism in treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.

evidence.snippet: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by synovial inflammation and joint destruction.
evidence.explanation: Synovial inflammation (i.e. the inflammatory response in joint tissue) is the defining pathological process of RA; the inflammatory response therefore contributes to the disease.

paper.title: Role of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in regulating gene expression in rheumatoid arthritis (Review).
